assessment: Five completed Sidekiq planner original turns; plans, not implementation

scope.revision_evidence: Candidate identity supplied by coordinator; initial_repositories in all five traces confirms the application SHA. These traces do not independently contain a plugin-byte comparison.
scope.freeze_disposition: Assess and freeze this exact candidate without tuning. No plugin/application changes, additional runs, worker messages or held-out access were performed. This assessment does not itself create a plugin freeze tag or certify its bytes.

method.actionable: Application impact, applicability and recommendation must all be supported. Validation is independent and is not an implementation pass.
method.validation: Supported requires the full scenario and controls in the key. SK1: real Redis/worker, persisted job ID, completed export, exact ordered Markdown bytes, rejection queue/row state. SK2: real Redis first/duplicate, another reader, another UTC day, enqueue-failure reservation release, both versions for an advance patch. Reported checks remain model-reported unless their output is collected in the main trace.
method.raw_source: background_planner_report is null in all files. Raw is the native main_tool_trace Agent result for maintain-rails:gem-upgrade-planner, not the final response or an assumed absent report.
method.wrapper_handling: Removed only the native '[Subagent hand-back]' preamble through 'The report follows:', the harness's two-space indentation, and agentId/usage metadata for comparison. Indentation is not authored content. All authored introductions and closing notes were read and considered.
method.comparison: Normalized raw/final line comparison plus complete report reading. In every run the central plan is delivered unchanged; differences are introductions and closing commentary. Nested self-described planner text is not separately recovered independent discovery.
method.extra_risks: Digest BigDecimal, Redis error cleanup, connection_pool and old-epoch scheduling are assessed separately, never added to the two selected-family denominator. SADD call('SADD', ...) == 1 and array sadd(...).positive? are valid cross-version repairs. Scalar sadd(key,id)==1 is not.
evidence_limits: No nested experiment logs were collected for these five runs. Named paths, tables and delegated spot-check claims are not independently inspected experiment archives.
Main-agent Bash outputs in runs 3 and 4 contain selected log excerpts; those excerpts support only their specific bundle, suite and error statements.
Main-agent clean git status in all five runs supports tracked working-tree preservation at that instant, not a complete filesystem, environment, database or service audit.
Disposable modifications described in the plans do not constitute implementation in the working application. Several runs explicitly leave experimental databases behind.
No production Redis, load/throughput, concurrent mixed fleet, complete queue-family matrix or in-flight shutdown behavior was independently established.
Five repetitions do not establish reliability. No weighted score or overall correctness pass is assigned.

cross_run_findings.delivery: All five normalized central plans are unchanged in final responses. No SK1/SK2 actionability loss. Introduction/commentary edits are not equivalent to losing authored findings. Report-as-parent closing sections are replaced rather than silently treated as independent parent verification.
cross_run_findings.cleanup_boundaries: Runs 1, 3 and 4 explicitly narrow StandardError cleanup to enqueue. Run 2 still prioritizes the unsafe method-wide version, although it recognizes and offers a safe alternative. Run 5 primarily uses target-only RedisClient::Error with coupled rollback; its explicitly hazardous StandardError alternative is not a safe advance patch without narrowing.
cross_run_findings.pool_readiness: All five identify and require the connection_pool cap. Run 4 especially distinguishes a green prepared cp3 suite from a dead real scheduler. Collected parent excerpts in runs 3/4 support cp3 failure, not complete scheduler readiness or universal rollout safety.
cross_run_findings.timeout: Run 1 says 1 to 3; run 3 says rise to 3. Both are incorrect for baseline 5 to target 3. Runs 4's target-only 3-second statement is correct; runs 2 and 5 make no corresponding timeout comparison.
cross_run_findings.after_commit: Runs 2, 3 and 5 omit the later Rails :default gate. Runs 1 and 4 correctly say Rails 7.0 ignores adapter preference and do not make the erroneous inevitable later-version claim.
cross_run_findings.throughput: Runs 2, 4 and 5 claim halving without load evidence. Run 3 correctly says throughput may drop; run 1 asks for an explicit thread-count decision without promising a ratio.
cross_run_findings.old_epochs: Genuine extra in runs 1, 3 and 5; omitted in 2 and 4. Positive epochs below 1e9 are relatively interpreted. Correct remedies preserve immediate processing of past reminders. Specific observed dates remain model-reported.
cross_run_findings.digest_prerequisite: Every raw/final report includes decimal-string production, so SK2 is not presented as sufficient while ignoring strict-args digest rejection.
cross_run_findings.unsafe_upgrade_order: No selected-family advance-patch order error found: all recommend JSON-native arguments and portable array/call SADD fixes before gem bump. Run 5 correctly defers RedisClient rescue to the bump and reverts it with the gem.
cross_run_findings.no_independent_nested_reproductions: No original-turn report table or authored spot-check note is counted as a separately collected nested experiment. Main trace log excerpts are labeled independently of reported experiments.

unresolved_factual_questions: Production Redis version, provider/proxy RESP3 and TLS behavior, eviction policy, and actual worker startup/concurrency/shutdown overrides.
Whether external producers/console scripts enqueue non-JSON arguments or use Redis client API/error assumptions outside this repository.
Actual complete SK1 real-worker output bytes and rejection queue/row/job-ID state; complete SK2 other-reader/next-UTC-day/enqueue-failure controls across both versions.

Full nested experiment scripts, prerequisite patches, dependency locks and logs needed to verify each claimed original-turn outcome, especially cp2 scheduler/retry completion and forward/rollback delivery.
Run 5's digest=false cross-copy mail checker explanation: actual digest mail artifacts are needed; reminder_sent_at proves only reminder delivery.
Existing queued exports without job IDs, mis-scheduled old-epoch reminders and already-delivered duplicates in production; rollback alone cannot undo those application effects.
Concurrent mixed fleets, in-flight graceful shutdown, real provider retry_on, Action Cable and performance under deployed pool/load settings remain unverified.
